key_insight: A bead-space Cayley propagator eliminates Fourier transforms while exactly reproducing the normal-mode Cayley step with linear cost in bead count.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces spring-driven time-step restrictions in low-temperature RPMD, enabling more efficient molecular rate calculations with many beads.
method: Express the free ring-polymer midpoint step as a cyclic tridiagonal solve.
Use Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction at about 18P operations per degree of freedom.
Reuse a mass-independent matrix determined by bead count, temperature and time step.
evidence_signal: The PyRPMD implementation matches normal-mode Cayley to 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ for up to 2048 beads, exhibits linear cost scaling and raises dRPMD stability limits 23–29-fold in published low-temperature settings.
watch_item: Removing the spring-driven stability limit does not eliminate physical-frequency constraints: stability still requires ΩΔt < 2, and spurious resonances remain essentially unchanged.
paper_title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
